_meta.purpose: Story micro-game DEFINITIONS, keyed by id. Renderers live in battle.html (StoryMiniGames); these are the tunable numbers the maintainer owns (rounds, tell odds, prompts, win/lose flavour). Attach a game to a scene via data/story/interactions.json (act-level) or via a STORY_BATTLE_INTERRUPTS challenge (battle-level). A micro-game is a SPICE, never a gate: losing never blocks progress. type ∈ 'rps' | 'tell' | 'memory' | 'riddle' | 'spot' | 'cipher' | 'craft'. DESIGN LAW: a signature is high interactivity, little/no mechanical effect — never a battle-MECHANIC change (softenBattle is deprecated/unused). Sanctioned effects: gold / item / flag / giftPokemon, and the RARE skipBattle (pacifist/ransom 'no fight' route). Balance numbers (gold, gift species) are maintainer-owned.

schema.rps: { type:'rps', rounds:int(best-of), tell:0..1(chance CPU plays tellThrow), tellThrow:0|1|2(rock|paper|scissors), title, prompt, winLine, loseLine, drawLine }
schema.tell: { type:'tell', title, tell:'NPC tell line', options:[{label, reply:[...]}], answer:int(correct index), winLine, loseLine }
schema.memory: { type:'memory', length:int, symbols:[emoji...], title, winLine, loseLine }
schema.riddle: { type:'riddle', title, intro:[lines], steps:[{ q, options:[{label, reply:[...]}], answer:int }], passN:int(default=all steps), winLine, loseLine }
schema.spot: { type:'spot', title, prompt, items:[{label, reply:[...]}|str], answer:int(the 'off' one), winLine, loseLine }
schema.cipher: { type:'cipher', title, clue, symbols:[str...], length:int, answer:[idx...], attempts:int(default 3), wrongLine, winLine, loseLine }
schema.craft: { type:'craft', title, gatherPrompt, ingredients:[str...], correct:[idx...], stepsPrompt, steps:[str...], stepOrder:[idx...], winLine, loseLine }

rps_route_punk.title: Rock · Paper · Scissors
rps_route_punk.prompt: The kid steps into the road with one fist up. “Two out of three and I move. You lose, we battle. Ready?”
rps_route_punk.winLine: He moves one boot out of your way. “Tell anybody I made you work for it.” No battle.
rps_route_punk.loseLine: He puts the fist in his pocket and brings out a Poké Ball. “All right. The other way.”
rps_route_punk.drawLine: He laughs through his nose. “We could do this all day. I’m getting cold. Battle?”

tell_rocket_grunt.title: Read the Tell
tell_rocket_grunt.tell: The Rocket grunt says the boss is out. He keeps one foot pushed against the warehouse door. A light goes out behind its window.

options.label: "Then you won't mind me checking that door."
reply: He lifts his foot. “Don't put my name down.”

options.label: "Sure. I'll be on my way."
reply: He looks back at the window only after you're gone.

options.label: "Where's your boss, really?"
reply: “He signs my clock card. You going to sign it?”

tell_rocket_grunt.winLine: He lifts his foot. There’s a dent in the side of his boot.
tell_rocket_grunt.loseLine: He puts his other foot against the door and fishes out a cigarette.

memory_hypno_trance.title: Hold the Pattern
memory_hypno_trance.winLine: You keep the last color in mind until the pendulum stops. You can hear the person next to you breathing again.
memory_hypno_trance.loseLine: The room comes back before the last color does. Both your hands are on the railing.

main_song_memory.title: The Song You Already Know
main_song_memory.winLine: You sing the last note early. A moment later it comes out of the speaker at the same pitch.
main_song_memory.loseLine: The tune finishes while you’re still waiting for the next note. You could swear it used to end differently.

main_dex_spot.title: The Entry That Wasn't There
main_dex_spot.prompt: Open your starter’s Pokédex entry. The print is still there. Which line was written by hand?

items.label: Habitat: temperate forests and the edges of towns.
reply: The print goes right into the page. You can't feel it under a nail.

items.label: Known for unwavering loyalty to a chosen trainer.
reply: You've read this exact sentence in three other entries.

items.label: You'll do this again. You always do this again.
reply: That is the way you join your letters when you're cold. There's a thumbprint on the back of the page.

items.label: Evolves through sustained companionship and training.
reply: An older trainer showed you how to turn to that field. It was already there.

main_dex_spot.winLine: You close it on your thumb. There’s ink on the side of your hand.
main_dex_spot.loseLine: The page refreshes. You almost remember the line that was there before.

main_first_riddle.title: Tell The First We Said Hi
intro: You called after the stranger, but the wind had picked up. He left you with one thing you could still hear.

steps.q: When the wind says 'The First,' who does the name fit?

options.label: A champion who came before me.
reply: Maybe. But the certainty in you isn't about a stranger.

options.label: Myself — in another life.
reply: The name sits down like you've worn it. On a peak just like this one. In your own voice, to someone smaller than you.

options.label: Someone I'm supposed to become.
reply: Warmer. The tense is wrong, but the dread is right.

main_first_riddle.winLine: You try saying the name aloud. You know which way to turn before you finish it.
main_first_riddle.loseLine: You let the name go. By the time the wind lets up, the road is empty.

main_count_cipher.title: The Plate Reads A Number
main_count_cipher.clue: Beside your name on the plate, someone has cut three digits into the metal. Enter the number you can see: 0 0 1.
main_count_cipher.wrongLine: That doesn’t match the plate. Try the three digits again.
main_count_cipher.winLine: The lock accepts 001. There’s a shallow mark on the 1 key where a fingernail kept hitting it.
main_count_cipher.loseLine: You take your hand off the buttons. The number stays lit.

tell_rocket_donated.title: Read the Old Man
tell_rocket_donated.tell: The old Rocket worker puts the list down and smooths the fold. DONATED TEST SUBJECTS. “I typed that,” he says. “There’s a carbon copy if you want to take one.”

options.label: "You want forgiveness."
reply: “I made sure the columns lined up. I don't know what you call that except helping.”

options.label: "You want a witness."
reply: “That's it. Keep the carbon dry. There's one name I never managed to spell properly.”

options.label: "You want me to act on it."
reply: “Do something if you can. First I need you to read the whole page.”

tell_rocket_donated.winLine: He lets you keep the carbon. He puts the sheet with the signatures back in his coat.
tell_rocket_donated.loseLine: He folds it along the old crease. The last name goes under his thumb.

riddle_magma_arithmetic.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
intro: The geologist has a map down on the floor. “The chamber will work,” he says. “I’ve seen it run twice.”
There are neat figures along the coast. Inland, where the people live, the paper is bare.

steps.q: Where does Magma's 'mercy' math actually break?

options.label: The numbers are wrong — the chamber won't ignite.
reply: 'No,' he says. 'The numbers are right. That's the whole horror of it.'

options.label: It counts the land and never once counts the people on it.
reply: He laughs, or sobs — hard to tell, this dry. 'There. They did the math a thousand times. Never once on the people.'

options.label: Mercy can't be put in an equation at all.
reply: 'A comfort,' he wheezes. 'But they'd only say you didn't run the numbers hard enough.'

riddle_magma_arithmetic.winLine: He circles the first house. You hold the paper flat while he finds the next one.
riddle_magma_arithmetic.loseLine: He starts at the left edge again. You can hear somebody knocking for him through the wall.

tell_aqua_fisherman.title: The Emptied Man
tell_aqua_fisherman.tell: The fisherman stands at the end of the empty mooring with a length of wet rope. “They left this.” He gets the knot halfway undone, then ties it again.

options.label: "Let me help you get a boat back."
reply: “I could get a boat. Nobody's put a stop to that.”

options.label: Say nothing. Step into the tide and stand with him.
reply: He slides one hand along the rope to make room for yours.

options.label: "It's not your fault."
reply: “That's what my sister says.” He tries the knot again.

tell_aqua_fisherman.winLine: After a while he offers you one end. You stay until the water turns around.
tell_aqua_fisherman.loseLine: He says thank you. By the time you’re up on the road he’s working the knot again.

memory_galactic_wall.title: Before They're Filed
memory_galactic_wall.winLine: You write down the order of the photographs before the new notices go up. You leave room beside each one for a name.
memory_galactic_wall.loseLine: The paste has taken. You can find the corners of the photographs through the paper.

spot_plasma_flyer.title: Who Told You
spot_plasma_flyer.prompt: WHO TOLD YOU THEY WANTED TO BE YOURS? The same Plasma flyer has gone up on every board. Who paid to print it?

items.label: The blue is Plasma's exact brand blue.
reply: True. But a colour isn't the tell.

items.label: Small print, bottom edge — sponsored by a foundation with Ghetsis's name on the masthead.
reply: There. The man asking who told you owns the press that prints the asking.
He doesn't need you to put the ball down. He just needs you to keep holding the question.

items.label: The font is expensive.
reply: It is. So is everything they do. Not the tell.

items.label: There's no answer printed anywhere on it.
reply: Of course not — the question was never meant to be answered. Keep looking for who profits from the asking.

spot_plasma_flyer.winLine: You copy the foundation’s name. A shopkeeper sees you writing and asks if you need a better pen.
spot_plasma_flyer.loseLine: The question’s easy to carry. You can still read it from the bus stop.

tell_flare_scientist.title: Why He's Shaking
tell_flare_scientist.tell: Your name’s on the list the Flare scientist hands you. His is underneath. “I checked the rest of it before I checked that,” he says. His hands won’t settle.

options.label: "Because you'll be killed for leaking this."
reply: “I spent all morning thinking that was the worst of it. Then I found the address they wanted me to report to.”

options.label: "Because it's so much worse when they want you to live."
reply: “Yes. They sent me a key. There's meant to be a room for me afterwards.”

options.label: "Because the weapon actually works."
reply: “It works. They asked me to sign the test sheet twice. I did.”

tell_flare_scientist.winLine: He sits down. For the first time he lets the list go.
tell_flare_scientist.loseLine: He takes the list back, careful when he reaches your name.

tell_skull_guzma.title: The Booth
tell_skull_guzma.tell: Guzma has the karaoke booth to himself. The song’s paused. He’s using the screen light to look at an old photo.

options.label: Step in. Tell him you see him.
reply: He puts the photo face down. “Booth's booked, pal.”

options.label: Let him have the booth. Walk on.
reply: You wait until you can go without crossing the rectangle of light from the booth.

options.label: Get a photo of the moment.
reply: Your screen lights up. He sees it reflected over the words of the song.

tell_skull_guzma.winLine: You let the door go gently. The song starts again just after the latch catches.
tell_skull_guzma.loseLine: Guzma sticks the photo in his pocket and turns the volume up.

spot_yell_posters.title: The Crack in the Wall
spot_yell_posters.prompt: Someone’s marked every poster of Marnie along the bus stops. See if any one of them has been left alone.

items.label: A shelter where the marker bled through to the back.
reply: Sloppy. But not the tell.

items.label: One poster, third row, where her face isn't crossed out at all.
reply: A miss. A single uncrossed face in a town of crossed ones.
Somebody wheat-pasted this for a paycheck and hesitated on exactly one. There's a person inside the machine. People can be reached.

items.label: The hashtag printed under every one.
reply: The brand's, yes — but brands don't hesitate. People do. Look again.

items.label: The record-label logo in the corner.
reply: Whose money it is. Not whose hands. Keep looking for the hands.

spot_yell_posters.winLine: On the way back you start looking at who’s holding the paste bucket.
spot_yell_posters.loseLine: The first bus pulls in. You’re still trying to take the whole wall in at once.

spot_macro_obituary.title: Read Every Page
spot_macro_obituary.prompt: “I framed it so people would read it,” the retired trainer says. Her career notice is printed in Macro Cosmos colors. Which word is she waiting for you to ask about?

items.label: "Beloved by fans across the region."
reply: Probably true, even. Not the lie.

items.label: "Retired voluntarily."
reply: 'That one,' she says when you point. 'I didn't write it. I signed something once that let them write it.'
'Read every page next time. There's always a page near the back about how you'll be remembered. That's the page that costs you.'

items.label: "A celebrated career."
reply: Theirs to inflate. Not the load-bearing lie.

items.label: The dates of her championship run.
reply: Accurate. The facts are never the lie. The framing is.

spot_macro_obituary.winLine: At “voluntarily” she puts her glasses on the table. “Good. Put that in whatever you write.”
spot_macro_obituary.loseLine: She puts the frame back up. It takes her two goes to find the hook.

craft_star_rota.title: The Kitchen Rota
craft_star_rota.gatherPrompt: The twelve-year-old runs the kitchen for fifteen kids. Three are out sick today. Pick the cooks who can actually cover tonight.
ingredients: The one who can only really make rice
The careful one who reads the recipe twice
The youngest — too small to reach the stove
craft_star_rota.stepsPrompt: Now set the order so nobody's swamped: who preps, who cooks, who closes.
steps: Careful one preps and reads the recipe aloud
Rice kid plates up and cleans down
craft_star_rota.winLine: The kid clips your rota to the fridge. Penny puts herself on Thursday when she thinks you aren’t looking.
craft_star_rota.loseLine: They thank you and stick the rota up. The kid takes out a pencil before you get to the door.

riddle_cubone_page.title: The Weight
intro: A child’s handwriting. “Mum says when she goes I have to wear hers. She let me try it and it kept slipping.”
There’s a new tear where the next page should be.

steps.q: It was torn by someone who couldn't bear it. Couldn't bear what?

options.label: What the next page said.
reply: Maybe. A thing too heavy to keep where you'd read it again.

options.label: That the next page stopped.
reply: Maybe. An unfinished sentence is its own kind of unbearable.

options.label: You can't tell which is worse — and that's the weight.
reply: Yes. The not-knowing is the inheritance. That's what 'remember the weight' was always going to mean.

riddle_cubone_page.winLine: You put the torn edge back under the others. It’s a light little thing to have to leave there.
riddle_cubone_page.loseLine: You put the page down. The two holes for the threading are the only bits that line up.

spot_yamask_faceless.title: Who Isn't Quite Right
spot_yamask_faceless.prompt: The man who asked you for directions had nowhere to put a mouth. Nobody else broke off talking. Look at the people in front of you now.

items.label: The trucker reading a newspaper upside down.
reply: He turns the paper around when he sees you looking. Keeps one finger on the same sentence.

items.label: The woman at the vending machine — smooth, with eyes set where a face would keep them.
reply: She presses the coin slot with a fingertip. Her face is smooth except for two eyes. You wait while she gets her change.

items.label: The kid kicking a can by the pumps.
reply: The kid looks up when the truck goes by. He's chewing his sleeve.

items.label: The clerk behind the counter.
reply: The clerk ties the loose end of her apron. You're staring. She notices.

spot_yamask_faceless.winLine: The woman turns her head toward you. The person behind her makes room without turning.
spot_yamask_faceless.loseLine: A can comes down hard in the machine. Nobody on that side of the room looks up.

memory_hypno_year.title: The Year They Lost
memory_hypno_year.winLine: You give the child back the things in the order they remember them. They ask if the candle was still lit.
memory_hypno_year.loseLine: They reach for the first thing again. You can’t tell how many times you’ve watched that hand move.

spot_phantump_register.title: The Handwriting Matches Yours
spot_phantump_register.prompt: The register’s soaked along the edges. The newest name was written yesterday. Which entry is it?

items.label: A name in faded brown ink, halfway down.
reply: Old. Decades old. Not yesterday's.

items.label: The last line — fresh ink, dated yesterday, in handwriting that's yours.
reply: Not similar. Yours. The exact slant, the way you cross your sevens.
You didn't write it. You check twice, and being sure is so much worse than doubting.

items.label: A name crossed out near the top.
reply: Someone changed their mind once. Not the one.

items.label: A blank line at the very end.
reply: Waiting — but empty. The entry you want is already filled, in your hand.

spot_phantump_register.winLine: You put one finger next to the date. It’s the way you write a seven when you’re in a hurry.
spot_phantump_register.loseLine: The notebook closes itself under its own weight. There’s still a pen on the string.

tell_mimikyu_shopkeeper.title: Didn't Feel Right
tell_mimikyu_shopkeeper.tell: The costume’s come back three times. On every ticket somebody wrote DIDN’T FEEL RIGHT. The shopkeeper polishes the buckle. “Parents always ask if they can get a refund.”

options.label: "Kids are particular. Find it a buyer."
reply: The shopkeeper puts the tag back. She can't quite get it through the old hole.

options.label: Take it down and try it on yourself.
reply: You've put one arm in before you feel a tug from inside the other sleeve.

options.label: Press: why did all three say the exact same words?
reply: “One of them said it was wearing her.” She sets the buckle down. “Is that how I'd say it if the dress was too tight?”

tell_mimikyu_shopkeeper.winLine: The shopkeeper takes it off the rail. It stays sitting up after she sets it down.
tell_mimikyu_shopkeeper.loseLine: She puts the tag back where the next family can read it.

spot_drifloon_board.title: The Board Is Full
spot_drifloon_board.prompt: LOST BALLOONS, says the sign. Each slip carries a child’s name and a date. What do the dates have in common?

items.label: The slips are layered over slips, years deep.
reply: The bottom layer is soft at the edges. A drawing of a balloon comes away on your finger.

items.label: The dates are weekly — regular as a bus schedule, no gaps, no missed weeks.
reply: Same day of the week. Whoever keeps it has left the bottom corner clear for another slip.

items.label: Some of the names are misspelled.
reply: One name was corrected in a different pencil. Two people must have stopped at that note.

items.label: The newest slip is this week's.
reply: You can still see the fold where somebody carried it here.

spot_drifloon_board.winLine: There’s room for another notice at the bottom. Someone’s already put a pin there.
spot_drifloon_board.loseLine: A passing parent stops to straighten one of the corners. The paper’s worn thin where they touch it.

tell_parasect_break.title: Who's Steering
tell_parasect_break.tell: The Paras walks a figure eight around a berry. Its front claws twitch toward the fruit every time it passes. The mushroom keeps a steady note.

options.label: It's training — drilling a route.
reply: Its middle feet pass through the same soft places in the dirt. It doesn't change pace when you stand in front of it.

options.label: The bug's choosing to. It finds the loop restful.
reply: For a moment you see the front claw reach out of line. The back legs pull it round anyway.

options.label: The mushroom is steering. The bug's opinion stopped being collected a while ago.
reply: The mushroom makes that steady sound, but the claws keep missing the berry. You bring it a little closer.

tell_parasect_break.winLine: You set the berry a little closer. The front claw reaches it on the next pass. The rest of the body keeps walking.
tell_parasect_break.loseLine: You hear the same note twice as you leave. It’s louder over the bare part of the path.

memory_mewtwo_future.title: Three Seconds Early
memory_mewtwo_future.winLine: You step over the patch of floor just before the light falls there. You don’t know how long it took you to decide.
memory_mewtwo_future.loseLine: The light falls before you move. When you turn to look, your shadow’s already on the wall.

tell_plasma_knights.title: The Reluctant Bridge
tell_plasma_knights.tell: The Plasma knight on the left holds his glove like he’s about to knock. “We’re supposed to stop you here,” he says. He hasn’t let a Pokémon out.

options.label: "You don't have to do this. Stand aside."
reply: “You heard them,” the left one says to his partner. “You can put the glove down.”

options.label: "Then fight me and get it over with."
reply: He looks almost relieved. He knows what to do with a challenge.

options.label: "Your apologies don't free anyone."
reply: The one on the right starts to answer. The other puts a hand on his shoulder and they take their places.

tell_plasma_knights.winLine: They wait for each other to move first. Then the one on the left takes a step back, and you can cross. No battle.
tell_plasma_knights.loseLine: The knight gives his partner a small nod. They take up their places.

rps_skull_standoff.title: Saving Face
rps_skull_standoff.prompt: The Skull grunts look over their shoulders. Their friends are watching. “Two out of three. You win, you walk. Lose and we battle. C’mon, throw.”
rps_skull_standoff.winLine: They call it a fix loud enough for their friends to hear. The shorter one holds the gate for you. No battle.
rps_skull_standoff.loseLine: “Hear that? Wanted a battle the whole time.” He takes his Ball out with both hands.
rps_skull_standoff.drawLine: “Fine. Reckon we got witnesses now, so we better battle.”
